title: Accelerated node synapse pipeline and KV warmth controller
creator: Asha Patel
description: Goal: reduce cold-start tail latency for Dedicated capacity by introducing a lightweight, per-node pre-staging pipeline ("synapse pipeline") that coordinates fast weight snapshot handoffs and a companion KV Warmth Controller that adaptively primes token KV caches based on live traffic signals. This ticket implements the runtime coordination layer, admission controller policies for pre-staging, and the initial heuristics for KV priming that balance start-up latency against memory and cross-tenant IO costs.
acceptance_criteria: Cold-start p50 for 2k token requests on a fresh node reduced by >= 30% in the lab benchmark compared to baseline
KV priming cost per prewarm action measured and capped (SLO): average extra memory IO <= 8% of node bandwidth for steady-state priming
Node pre-stage protocol supports partial snapshot handoff (layers 0..N) and resumes without full re-download on interrupted handoffs
Controller exposes metrics: prewarm_attempts, prewarm_success_rate, avg_prewarm_io_bytes, kv_hit_rate_post_prewarm
No regression on throughput targets for Dedicated fleets under baseline traffic (<= 5% variance)
E2E tests and one canary deployment plan documented in linked GH PR and Confluence doc
implementation_notes: Component: Synapse pre-stage agent runs in node init; lightweight coordinator talks to controller via control-plane API (gRPC with auth token)
Snapshot format: incremental shard deltas + layer manifests to allow partial handoffs and resume-on-fail semantics
Admission: soft quotas per-tenant and per-fleet to avoid IO storms; controller applies backpressure and burst windows
KV priming heuristic: seed top-k recent prefixes observed on tenant routers + probabilistic token-level warming to limit IO; fallback to on-demand warm if budget exceeded

Trade-off considered: aggressive full-model prefetch reduces latency but increases cold-start churn and cost; we choose a mixed strategy (critical layers first + selective KV) for best amortized unit cost
Rollback plan: disable controller by flag, revert pre-stage scheduling, and allow nodes to start in conservative mode
Observability: ship new Grafana dashboards and add tracing spans for handoff steps; sample raw priming traces to S3 for 7 days
Security: use per-node mTLS for control-plane RPCs; no model weights leave node network boundary except via authenticated snapshot transfers
